title: U.S. House · New York's 16th District
area: Parts of the northern Bronx (Riverdale, Wakefield, Woodlawn) and most of Westchester County, including Yonkers, Mount Vernon, New Rochelle, and White Plains.

context.text: Both the Democratic primary (incumbent George Latimer) and the Republican primary (Joseph Cinquemani) were canceled; each candidate advanced to the general election unopposed.
John Franklin Wilson IV, who had been listed as an Independent candidate, withdrew or was disqualified and does not appear on the November 3 general-election ballot, leaving a two-candidate race.
Latimer won the seat in 2024 by defeating incumbent Rep. Jamaal Bowman in the Democratic primary, 58.6%–41.4%, before winning the general election.

candidates.name: George Latimer
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative, NY-16 (since 2025); former Westchester County Executive (2018–2025)

summary.text: Latimer is a Westchester native who worked as a marketing executive before more than three decades in elected office: Rye City Council, the Westchester County Board of Legislators, the State Assembly, the State Senate, and Westchester County Executive from 2018. He won the 2024 Democratic primary over incumbent Rep. Jamaal Bowman and has represented NY-16 since January 2025. He serves on the House Foreign Affairs and Small Business Committees and has introduced bills on election interference, small-business research funding, and electric-vehicle battery safety.

background.text: Born November 22, 1953, in Mount Vernon, New York, and describes himself as a third-generation Westchester native, according to his official biography. He graduated from Mount Vernon High School in 1970.
Earned a B.A. from Fordham University in 1974 (history and theology, per Ballotpedia) and a Master of Public Administration from New York University's Wagner School in 1976.
Worked for more than 20 years as a marketing executive at corporate subsidiaries of Nestle and ITT, according to his official biography; Ballotpedia also lists Benchmark Hospitality.

Won his first race for public office in 1987, a seat on the Rye City Council. In 1991 he was elected to the Westchester County Board of Legislators, becoming the first Democrat to win the 7th District seat; he served until 2004, including as Minority Leader and as the board's first Democratic chairman.

Elected to the New York State Assembly in 2004 and, according to his official biography, authored more than 20 new laws there. Elected to the State Senate in November 2012, representing the 37th District, and served until 2017.
Elected Westchester County Executive in 2017 and took office in January 2018 as the county's ninth County Executive; re-elected in November 2021.
Defeated incumbent Rep. Jamaal Bowman in the June 25, 2024 Democratic primary, 58.6% to 41.4%, and won the general election that November over Republican Miriam Flisser, 71.3% to 28.3%.

Serves on the House Foreign Affairs Committee and the House Small Business Committee, and belongs to the Congressional Labor Caucus, Congressional Reproductive Freedom Caucus, Equality Caucus, New Democrat Coalition, and Sustainable Energy and Environment Coalition.

priorities.text: "George Latimer understands it is only by lifting each other up that we all rise together... addressing the availability of affordable housing has been and will continue to remain a top priority."
"Latimer will continue to prioritize keeping our communities safe by advocating for gun reform including an assault weapons ban and universal background checks."
"George will be an advocate for combating climate change, investing in renewable energy sources to transition away from fossil fuels, and creating sustainable green jobs."
"George is deeply committed to continue these efforts and can assure you that he will protect Medicare and Social Security from being dismantled."

positions.summary: Latimer says he will fight national abortion bans and vote for the Women's Health Protection Act to protect clinic access and reproductive rights.
positions.quote: committed to ensuring clinic access and defending healthcare providers who offer reproductive services, and if elected will seek to secure these rights and protections by voting for the Women's Health Protection Act. Additionally, in Congress, George will fight back against any efforts to pass a national abortion ban, he will advocate for expanding access to contraception and preserving options such as in vitro fertilization (IVF) to empower individuals in family planning decisions.

positions.summary: Latimer supports an assault weapons ban, universal background checks, and ERPOs (state 'red flag' orders) to temporarily restrict firearm access for people in crisis.
positions.quote: Latimer will continue to prioritize keeping our communities safe by advocating for gun reform including an assault weapons ban and universal background checks.

positions.summary: Latimer says he will advocate for renewable energy investment and support a Green New Deal.
positions.quote: George will be an advocate for combating climate change, investing in renewable energy sources to transition away from fossil fuels, and creating sustainable green jobs... he will support passing a Green New Deal.

positions.summary: Latimer's platform commits to 'protecting renters' rights' alongside incentivizing affordable housing construction.
positions.quote: Latimer will maintain his commitment to push for the implementation of policies that address the root causes of the housing crisis, which includes incentivizing the construction of affordable housing units... as well as protecting renters' rights, and expanding access to homeownership opportunities for low and middle-income families.

positions.summary: Latimer says he will continue to stand with Israel's right to self-defense while advocating for a two-state solution.
positions.quote: George will continue to stand with Israel and support its rights of existence, stability, self-defense, and peace – and will advocate for a two-state solution among Israelis and Palestinians.

positions.summary: Latimer supports comprehensive immigration reform focused on work permits and a path to citizenship rather than expanded enforcement, and says he helped house asylum seekers as County Executive.
positions.quote: As a candidate for Congress, Latimer firmly advocates for supporting comprehensive immigration reform... George will prioritize accelerating work permits for immigrants to contribute to our economy while creating a fair and accessible path to citizenship.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Foreign Affairs and the House Committee on Small Business, 119th Congress.

Introduced the POINT Act (Protecting Our Integrity and Nation from Tyranny Act) on March 11, 2026, to prevent the President or any executive-branch agent from attempting to influence or prevent the administration of a U.S. election.
Introduced the SBIR Administrative Funding Act on January 23, 2026, to support long-term agency planning and coordination for the Small Business Innovation Research program.

Introduced the Electric and Hybrid Vehicle Battery Safety Act of 2026 with Rep. Brian Fitzpatrick (R-PA) on January 23, 2026, bipartisan legislation to reduce the risk of injury and death from EV and hybrid battery fires.

Co-sponsored the Families Deserve to Know Act with Rep. Ritchie Torres (NY-15), introduced August 13, 2026, which would require ICE to notify a detained person's family of a death or medical emergency in custody.

candidates.name: Joseph Cinquemani
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced unopposed after the Republican primary was canceled
candidates.currentRole: Attorney, Law Office of Joseph Cinquemani (New Rochelle)

summary.text: Cinquemani is a New Rochelle attorney who has practiced real estate and business law for more than 25 years and is the Republican nominee for NY-16. According to his campaign website, he has lived in New Rochelle and Pelham Bay for 30 years. He is running on tax relief, lower energy costs, reduced federal spending, and what he describes as pro-worker, pro-union job creation, and opposes what he calls 'deprivation, division, and despair' ideologies.

background.text: Graduated from Pearl River High School, according to Ballotpedia, and earned a B.S. from Cornell University's School of Industrial and Labor Relations in 1990 and a J.D. from Fordham University School of Law in 1994.
Admitted to the New York State Bar in 1995 and to practice before the U.S. District Courts for the Eastern and Southern Districts of New York; holds a real estate broker license.

Has operated the Law Office of Joseph Cinquemani, Esq., in New Rochelle since October 1997, representing clients in business, real estate, and secured transactions, including start-ups and cannabis businesses. His campaign biography describes a practice focused on real estate, business transactions, and succession planning.

Serves on the New York State Bar Association's Cannabis Law Section Committee and is a member of the Fordham Law and Cornell alumni associations; he and his family volunteer with Hope & Heroes, which raises funds for childhood cancer and blood disorder care.
Became the Republican nominee for NY-16 in 2026 after the June 23 Republican primary was canceled.
According to his campaign website, he has lived in New Rochelle and Pelham Bay for 30 years and is the father of triplets who attended New Rochelle public schools.

priorities.text: His campaign lists objectives of "tax relief, lower energy costs, to create high-paying union jobs, cut the budget, tame inflation, and lower interest rates to make housing more affordable."
"The American worker is the backbone of our economy," with an emphasis on promoting union trades as an alternative to costly college degrees.

positions.summary: Campaign energy page backs recommissioning Indian Point with small modular reactors, reopening New York to natural gas extraction, and the call to "Drill, baby, drill!".

candidates.researchNotes: Cinquemani has not completed Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey and has reported no FEC receipts as of the most recent filing period; positions above come entirely from his own campaign website.

statements.quote: cutting administrative costs and eliminating unnecessary regulation to encourage market forces to build housing and an improved health care system.
